contains.spu_object_hit_admission_613: REWINDBOX_SPU_OBJECT_HIT_ADMISSION_613 (SPULLVMRecompiler.cpp compile()): the SPU object cache is read and validated before the LLVM compile admission; a hit of a block of at most 16 KiB no longer takes the admission (128 MiB minimum per job, at most 3 jobs, 1 under pressure); a miss, a rejected object or a larger block is admitted as before. contains.zcull_sync_probe_613: REWINDBOX_ZCULL_SYNC_PROBE_613 (VKGSRender.cpp, IOSRsxSyncProfile.h, RPCS3IOSPerformance.cpp): measurement only. COREPROF ZCULLSYNC613 reports per window the ZCULL report reads that gathered occlusion queries (count:total_ms:max_ms, submission and MoltenVK wait included), the reads that had to submit the open command buffer, the zcull_sync hints that submitted ahead of a read, and precise/relaxed. contains.core613_20261102: the Core 613 record (Core 612 record, SPU object-hit admission, ZCULL report-read probe), unchanged in behaviour; build-utils/rpcs3/core616-from-613.patch (insertions only) turns its files into the Core 616 files
contains.zcull_poll_no_wait_616: REWINDBOX_ZCULL_POLL_NO_WAIT_616 (VKGSRender.cpp check_occlusion_query_status): a non-forced ZCULL poll reports a query ready only when gathering its host queries (one per command buffer it spans, oldest first until the first hit, all of them in precise mode) will not wait for the GPU; upstream checks only the oldest one, so a poll whose oldest part found no hit waited in MoltenVK for the command buffer a zcull_sync hint had just submitted. Same values, same report order (the poll still stops at the first query not ready), forced reads (sync, read barriers, conditional render) unchanged. Assassin's Creed Build 614 logs (PID 64664, windows 20-33): 4.1-4.4 s of every 5 s window inside report reads whatever their number (31,500-48,300), result_flushes 0, hint_flushes equal to the submissions; frame time fits 24.2 ms + 8.7 us per draw + 0.655 ms per submitted command buffer (R2 0.937, windows 12-37)
contains.zcull_wait_probe_616: REWINDBOX_ZCULL_WAIT_PROBE_616 (VKQueryPool.cpp, RSXZCULL.cpp, RSXThread.cpp, IOSRsxSyncProfile.h, RPCS3IOSPerformance.cpp): measurement only. COREPROF ZCULLWAIT616 splits the MoltenVK wait (vkGetQueryPoolResults with WAIT) by the path that asked for the result (poll, forced read, conditional render, sync), counts the gathers per path and the polls the 616 change deferred
contains.zclip_window_z_616: REWINDBOX_ZCLIP_WINDOW_Z_616 (RSXVertexPrologue.glsl, GLSLTypes.h, GLSLCommon.cpp, VKVertexProgram.cpp, title lever): Black Ops II (BLES01717) only. Without float64 nor an unrestricted depth range (MoltenVK) the vertex fallback compresses Z above 1 into [0.99, 1] from window Z (d) instead of clip-space Z (pos.z). The BLES01717 capture of RPCS3 issue #13227 draws 26 of 4,023 draws with clip [1, 1e19], viewport Z scale 1e19 over offset 1, reversed depth GEQUAL (12-draw depth prepass, 12-draw colour pass, 2 blended); the upstream fallback gives every fragment of those draws depth 1.0 (host test), so the colour pass keeps the last triangle drawn instead of the nearest; with window Z the depth follows the view distance (1.0 to 0.9901). The SPIR-V of every other title is byte-identical (glslang); Black Ops II vertex Metal libraries are compiled again once
contains.spu_object_prefetch_616: REWINDBOX_SPU_OBJECT_PREFETCH_616 (ios/IOSSpuObjectPrefetch.h, JITLLVM.cpp, SPUCommonRecompiler.cpp, System.cpp, title lever): Black Ops II (BLES01717) only. After the SPU object-cache eviction plan, one utility-class thread reads the title's compressed objects into memory (newest first, 48 MiB budget, objects up to 256 KiB); a compile thread takes an object's bytes once and inflates and validates them as after its own read; an object not read yet is claimed and read from disk as before, never awaited; the store is emptied when emulation stops. Build 614 logs: 7,162 object reads (4,300.8 ms, 0.6 ms each) in the first window of a multiplayer match with the 2,038.7 ms frame 2388, and a 613-read burst with the 1,121.4 ms frame 3537, both without a blocking pipeline. JITCacheCompatibility.cmake maps the exact JITLLVM.cpp and SPUCommonRecompiler.cpp to their delivered Core 613 effective hashes
